messages:
liz_h: noticed a weird pattern — multiple sessions for user svc-deploy showed immediate session_revoke within 1s of creation across 3 regions, no MFA challenge logged. anyone else seeing this?
matt_s: I see it, pulled logs for svc-deploy-aws-role. Looks like token exchange succeeded then gateway issued revoke
samir_r: do we have an IP/UA pattern? could be legitimate infra job?
liz_h: UA is empty for two events and "curl/7.8" for one. IPs are rotated cloud proxies, not our known infra pool
sec-bot: alert: SSO session_revocation_rate spike for tenant:redwood-prod — 3 events in 2m (severity: medium)
oncall-sre: paging oncall in case it's automation loop, @matt_s can you check key rotations/KMS access?
matt_s: checking KMS logs — no customer master key rotations at that time. but I see a `sts:AssumeRole` followed by `RevokeSession` call from our sso-proxy
samir_r: paste log snippet: `2026-03-19T03:14:22Z svc-deploy assumed role arn:... via sso-proxy; 03:14:22.2 RevokeSession token_id=abcd... reason=policy:cred_handoff`
liz_h: policy:cred_handoff? we've never used that reason code before — might be new from upstream auth lib
matt_s: grep shows a recent deploy of auth-lib 2.7.0 that added heuristics to invalidate sessions when source UA missing. Could be overly aggressive
oncall-sre: containment proposal: block the sso-proxy instance group from issuing revoke until we confirm
samir_r: agree, but let's throttle rather than full block. add a deny rule on revoke for service accounts with tag `infra:true`
liz_h: created temporary ACL in gateway: deny revokes from sso-proxy to roles with tag infra:true — applied to prod region A and B
matt_s: reverting auth-lib side change on canary to remove the new heuristic, and rolling back 2.7.0 -> 2.6.9
sec-bot: deploybot: rollback auth-lib v2.7.0 -> v2.6.9 started by @matt_s (canary)
matt_s: canary looks clean, revoke events stopped on canary host. rolling to remaining hosts in 10m window
liz_h: notify support/eng infra & customers if any service jobs impacted by temporary ACL? We should avoid hitting runbooks yet.
oncall-sre: opening incident ticket INC-20260319-42, will post incident summary there and link to audits
samir_r: postmortem items: 1) add test for empty UA flows 2) add structured reason codes to revokes 3) add RBAC rule to protect infra-tagged roles 4) KMS audit integration to flag revokes from proxies
liz_h: I will draft comms for impacted teams and update the SSO runbook with the fix steps and rollback procedure
matt_s: good — I'll include the auth-lib PR and changelog in the ticket. Also recommend a temporary monitoring alert for `policy:cred_handoff` reasons
sec-bot: action: assign INC-20260319-42 to sec@redwood with severity medium
liz_h: thanks everyone — will follow up with incident summary and timeline in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
